exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 4028 preterm twin offspring (1703 vaginally delivered and 2325 by cesarean section), excluding cases with congenital malformations or perinatal deaths.
finding: Cesarean delivery in preterm twins was associated with a higher incidence of long-term respiratory, neurologic, and infectious morbidities, with gastrointestinal morbidities also more pronounced but not reaching statistical significance in multivariable analysis.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery in preterm twins was associated with an increased incidence of long-term respiratory, neurologic, infectious, and gastrointestinal morbidities compared to vaginal delivery, suggesting potential benefits of vaginal delivery.
